answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 5 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The river multiplier is published, charged in umber, and juniper lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2452 identities would post 1483 proofs and burn roughly 11 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
